name: Visual Quality of a Historic High Street over Time (Bursa)
description:
Method replication: participants score 6 facade images of Atatürk Street, Bursa, on the paper's six visual quality indicators (greenery, openness, enclosure, imageability, complexity, walkability) from 1 (lowest impression) to 5 (highest), with each indicator's definition shown; the caption gives the point on the street, the side and the capture date. The images are not the paper's stimuli (69 Google Street View facade views fetched for this template: north and south facades at 12 points about 50 m apart, each in 2014, 2020 and 2022–2024, so changes at the same point can be compared).
Original study: Gönül & Durak (2025), "On measuring the change in historical city centres: an attempt at comparing human perception and deep learning through visual quality of street space", Multimedia Tools and Applications 84, 39283–39305. Along Atatürk High Street beside the UNESCO-listed Khans Area, 27 points 50 m apart were photographed in 2014, 2018, 2020 and 2023. Semantic segmentation of 360° panoramas measured the six indicators, and six experts (architects, urban planners, landscape architects) and eight stakeholders scored the facade images of 2014, 2020 and 2023 on a 5-point scale, after first viewing all facades together and picking the best and worst point for each indicator.
Differences from the original study: (1) 12 points over about 750 m of the street instead of 27 over the full study section; (2) the third year is the newest Street View available at each point (2022 at most points, 2024 at one) instead of 2023, and one point's first year is 2015; (3) each participant scores 6 random images on all indicators at once, instead of scoring every facade indicator by indicator after the best/worst calibration step; (4) open to anyone, with a question on the participant's role; (5) indicator definitions are short summaries of the paper's definitions.
author: Gönül & Durak

choices.text: Local stakeholder (government, neighbourhood or trade representative)

elements.name: visual_quality
elements.title: Score this facade image on each indicator (1–5)

dimensions.label: Greenery: Trees, shrubs and other plants visible in the street
Openness: How much open space and sky you can see; how much light reaches the street
Enclosure: How strongly the street is enclosed and defined by building facades, trees or walls
Imageability: How distinctive, recognisable and memorable the place is (historic buildings, landmarks, vistas)
Complexity: Visual richness and variety: buildings, facade details, plants, street furniture, signs, people
Walkability: How safe, comfortable and attractive the street is for walking
